title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek baked aubergine and lamb with béchamel
excerpt: Layers of fried aubergine, spiced lamb mince, and a thick béchamel sauce baked together until golden and set. The definitive Greek baked dish, warming and deeply savoury, built in stages and worth every step.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is eaten across the Middle East and the Balkans in many variations. The Greek version with béchamel was standardised by Nikolaos Tselementes, a Greek chef who trained in France and published influential Greek cookbooks in the 1920s and 1930s. His addition of the French béchamel topping transformed a simpler layered vegetable and meat dish into the rich, oven-baked casserole that is now considered definitively Greek. The aubergine slices are traditionally fried in olive oil before layering; some cooks grill them instead to reduce the oil. The béchamel must be very thick so it does not sink into the filling during baking, and must be seasoned with nutmeg.

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices and leave to drain for 30 minutes, then rinse and dry thoroughly before frying. Fry in batches without crowding; they should be golden and completely tender before layering. The béchamel must be thick enough to hold its own weight on top of the filling without spreading through the layers.

items.preparation: sliced 1 cm thick; salted and rinsed
or kefalotyri; grated; for the topping

content.text: Fry the dried aubergine slices in batches in olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and soft. Drain on kitchen paper.
Brown the mince with the onion and garlic. Add the wine, tomato puree, tinned tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, and oregano. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until very thick, about 8 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the nutmeg, season, then stir in the beaten eggs quickly.

Heat the oven to 180°C / fan 160°C / gas 4. Layer half the aubergine in a large baking dish. Add all the meat sauce. Layer the remaining aubergine on top. Pour the béchamel over and spread evenly. Scatter with grated cheese. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden on top and set. Leave to cool for 10 minutes before cutting.
